speaker: Anchor
line_text: Board the Strahl? (choices: Yes / No) / Boarding will dismiss your Esper. Proceed? (choices: Yes / No) / Boarding will cause you to dismount. Proceed? (choices: Yes / No)

speaker: Caravaner
line_text: Hello there, you a traveler? Well, traveler, you've found Adair's Caravan, bringing dreams, and bringing wares to every corner of the land. The Mosphoran Highwaste is a harsh place, son. You need something, you speak with Luccio. / Hello there. Welcome to Adair's Caravan, bringing dreams, and bringing wares to every corner of the land. Crossing the mountains, are you? Rest here a while, it's a long way yet. You need something, you speak with Luccio. / Hello there, traveler. Listen close, and I'll let you in on a secret: there's a path on this mountain you need a chocobo to access. Quite handy, too. Ach, sorry, but I can't lend you one of mine. These are for the caravan. Can't move wares if you can't move, eh? If you've some gysahl greens on you, you might try riding a wild chocobo. I saw one just northeast up the mountain.

speaker: Caravaner
line_text: Crossing the mountain, boy? Take care: a great slaven wilder, an atomos, has been seen raging up ahead, just before the Salikawood. It's a real nuisance. We've an order to fill from Burrogh in Nalbina, and we can't get there. In Adair's Caravan, our motto is "what you want, when you want it." Doesn't do to keep a customer waiting... / Hello, boy. I saw you take down that atomos. I feel sorry for the thing, but it had to be done. Well, now, you headed over the mountain, boy? It's a long journey, you might want to rest up here first. You need anything, talk to Luccio. / Take care, boy. We've heard reports of a great slaven wilder, an atomos, raging up ahead, just before the Salikawood. It's a real nuisance. We've an order to fill from Burrogh in Nalbina, and we can't get there. In Adair's Caravan, our motto is "what you want, when you want it." Doesn't do to keep a customer waiting... / Hello, boy. I saw you take down that atomos. I feel sorry for the thing, but it had to be done. Well, I'm off to get those goods for Burrogh. Some kind of crafted thing, not even really sure what it is. No matter, I'm off!

speaker: Adair
line_text: I'll admit, when the water started flowing from the shrine, I was surprised. Take a look, boy, it's quite beautiful. That one over there, he's come all the way from Archades to visit this shrine and learn its secrets. / You're a spirited one to travel on these mountain roads, boy. Keep it up and I might invite you to join my caravan one day. Ha ha ha! You probably think the idea of the land caravan quaint, but airships are no good for reaching the tucked-away places. We're needed. / You're a spirited one to walk these mountain roads, boy. Misplaced your airship, perhaps? Ha ha ha! About the only ones traveling on foot these days are those without two coins to rub together, dyed-in-the-wool travelers, or else... But I don't mean to pry, and I won't. Going to Archadia? You'll want to cross the mountains to the north, then go east through the forest. / The gate between the Phon Coast and the Salikawood has been repaired. This will make life easier. Or do you think travel by road a chore? Maybe we think trading isn't all about efficiency... Maybe we like it better this way.

Greetin's there, sonny. Anything you need, you let me know. 'Course, you gotta pay. Heh heh. / The beasts 'round here are of the most violent sort you might hope to find in the mountains. Go prepared, or don't go at all. / Well now, you goin' to the capital? It's a long way. Best get what you need now, or you'll regret it later. / With the Salika gate fixed, we should see more travel to Mosphora. If there's one thing I know, it's roads bring people.

speaker: Va'Kansa
line_text: I got separated from me partner, y'see. Caravan's taken me in, till I get back on my feet. / I've walked this way too many times to count, procuring wares in Archadia...'cept I never lost my partner before this time. / I got a baaaad feeling about this... Might be time to post a bill for one of them—what were they called? Marks? Eh? Sorry, don't mind me. / I was put out by my foreman, nowhere to go... when the caravan invited me along. I thought they were the nicest, kindest people in Ivalice...and then they told me I had to work for free to pay for all the food.

speaker: Va'Kansa
line_text: Eeeh? Keep it down, man. I'm busy here, can't you see? If you've no business with me, I'll speak with you later. Or...did you come about the Braegh? (choices: That's right. / Wrong.) / Eh? Truly? Heh. Sorry I tried to brush you off, there. Now, listen up. I'm a traveling merchant, see. Me and my partner were on our way out to the Hunter's Camp on the Phon Coast with some wares. Thing is, we took a wrong turn in the Salikawood. A bad turn. That's when we ran into that nightmare... Talk about "wild horses"! I escaped by the bristles on my chin...but when I came back, my partner and our wares were gone! I thought I'd wait here for my partner, but so far I ain't seen hide nor hair of him. I'm worried... but not enough to go looking myself! That's why I posted that bill, and why I want you to go get that Braegh for me! / The Braegh came upon us in the northwest of the Salikawood...pretty close to the Necrohol of Nabudis, come to think. Yeah, I know, the complete opposite direction from the Phon Coast, where we were supposed to be headed. / Hrrm? No? Bah. / Ran into a fearsome beast while porting some wares, and got separated from my partner... and I'm too scared to go looking for him! The Braegh came upon us in the northwest of the Salikawood...pretty close to the Necrohol of Nabudis. He's probably still there. / Ho hoh! (snort) You kill the Braegh? Here, your reward. / Hope my partner comes back safe... Eh? You want me to go look for him? No thanks! The Salikawood is no place I fancy going alone. Here I'm supposed to bring my wares to the Hunter's Camp on the Phon Coast, and I'm lacking both partner and wares! / Here I'm supposed to bring my wares to the Hunter's Camp on the Phon Coast, but my partner's nowhere to be found! Where could he be...? We've got a schedule to keep! / Whaaat? You met my partner on the Phon Coast? He got tired of waiting in the wood and went ahead, without me!? I was waiting for him! What, a message!? I'm fired!? Whaaaaaaaaaaaaa! / What'll I do now...? Maybe they've a spot for me on this caravan?

speaker: Caravaner
line_text: There're wild chocobos on this mountain. Saw one just up to the northeast. Think the wild ones are tougher than the domestics? / I've seen some wild chocobos on this mountain, up to the northeast. I hear if you feed 'em good they'll even let you ride 'em. A wild chocobo for a mount could make a hard trip easy... 'Course, you'd still have boulders to contend with. What to do with those... / Now that's just the thing. Caravan life ain't easy, but you take in a view like this, and it's all worth it.

speaker: Caravaner
line_text: The fellow studying these shrines headed up towards the peak. Said it's the closest place to the sky in the land. Romantic, eh? He's the one that told me about floatweed. Care to know? I'll tell you. (choices: Tell me. / No, thanks.) / See, when you touch one of the shrines 'round here, steam comes roilin' out of the spring, and the floatweed around it reacts, risin' up. Pretty soon, you've got yourself a path of floatin' floatweed. Thing is, you can only have three shrines putting out steam at once. As soon as you start fooling around with the fourth, all the floatweed drifts back down. One other thing he said. The shrine in the north- west don't do nothin'. Either it's got nothing to do with the 'weed, or it's broke. Who knows? / Right. Well, you change your mind, you know who to come to. / Care to hear about the shrines and the floatweed? (choices: Tell me. / No, thanks.) / The fellow who was checking out the shrines has headed up to the peak. Says that's the closest place to the sky in this land. / Quite a few shrines on this mountain. Built to worship some water god, from the looks of it. / One of the old shrines up here still gets water. I wonder why none of the others do? / One of the old shrines up here always had water. So I started wondering why none of the others did... No sooner did I have the thought than water started bubbling from the rest of the shrines! Weren't I surprised! This fellow here says the shrine waters have something to do with a road to a hidden place in the Mosphoran Highwaste... Intriguing, eh?

speaker: Learned Man; Viera Wayfarer
line_text: I'm on a journey to track down legends of the old gods. It is said a great holy tree sleeps on the peak of this mountain. You...you are not an ordinary hume, I feel. I sense great power about you. A strange aura, not of Man. / I've come from the capital to study the shrines here. They seem to be manufacted springs, in fact, drawing water up from an aquifer. Pity they seem to have dried up some time ago. / I've come from the capital to study the shrines here. They seem to be manufacted springs, in fact, drawing water up from an aquifer. Pity they seem to have dried up some time ago. The odd thing is, when I examined the shrines, the mechanisms seemed functional... Perhaps the flow of water underground changed? Perhaps it might change again? / Behold, water has returned to the parched shrines! I still don't know how the flow came back, but this clears up a few mysteries. Would you care to hear my theory? (choices: Listen / Leave) / Previously, I believed these shrines were a sort of artificial spring, meant to deliver water to these mountains. How wrong I was! In fact, when water is flowing to the shrines, touching a shrine just so causes the temperature of the water to rise quite dramatically. The steam from this...that's what lifts up the floatweed around the shrines! Floating up like balloons...floating on the air itself... It's a characteristic of the floatweed that makes it react to the steam so. In fact, I believe the shrines were made for no other purpose. With me so far? (choices: I'm with you. / Come again?) / Then allow me to continue. I ask: for what purpose might we want to float floatweed? Floatweed is a sturdy sort of shrub. When floating, several people can stand on it quite securely. Now, a book I read back in Archades said that floatweed was sometimes used to bridge gaps between rocks and such on mountain paths. I believe that here, in Mosphora, someone attempted to do the very same thing! Fascinating, don't you think? In documents on the Mosphoran Highwaste, one often hears of a place whose name translates roughly to the "wind-blown wyrm-god path." I had always wondered what it meant, and now I think it means the path's made of floatweed! And at the end of the path of the gods...heaven! In other words, this was all a way to make a path to the summit...that's my theory, at least. So, did you follow all that? (choices: I followed. / One more time?) / Unfortunately, I still can't find the route to the summit. Perhaps there's a trick to using the floatweed, or perhaps something else is needed... One thing's for sure, I shall get to the bottom of this! ...A-And then the top. Obviously. / I see, that's...too bad. It really is quite interesting, you know. / There's a deep connection between the floatweed and the shrines... Would you like to hear about it? (choices: Why not? / Nope.) / Touch a shrine, and steam comes out of the spring. In response, the surrounding floatweed rises, creating a path between cliffs and rocks. However, only three shrines may emit steam at one time. When a fourth is activated, the floatweed goes back down. I assume this is due to some limit on the amount of steam the shrines may produce. Line the floatweed up just so, and you could create a new road into the mountains. Myself, I'm aiming for the summit! / Very well. Just tap me on the shoulder should you change your mind.

speaker: Scout
line_text: Hello there! I'm a scout, a guide to this Mosphoran Highwaste. If there's anything you'd like to know, just ask! (choices: Ask about Mosphoran highlights. / Ask about the Mosphora region. / Ask about the scouts.) / The Mosphoran Highwaste is known for its oddly shaped rock formations. Some form roofs over the paths, or spires, or any number of other things. Also, right where you're standing is a spring, and resting place for travelers. The spring shrines antedate the Galtean Alliance! There is a lot we don't know about the shrines, even what their names mean. Some think they're shrines to wyrms, or water gods. All this and more awaits you in the Mosphoran Highwaste! / The Mosphoran Highwaste is a rugged, mountainous region, a natural border between Dalmasca and Nabradia. The climate changes greatly from the north to south sides. To the north of Mosphora you have a great forest, to the south a barren desert. Incidentally, how long do you think that guy is going to stand there? He keeps talking about making something of himself in the capital... But I haven't seen him take the smallest step towards Archades. Funny, the gate that way is fixed now 'n' everything. Maybe he's given up? / Like I said, we scouts are guides to the mountain. We know more about the Mosphoran Highwaste than anyone, and we're proud of it! / The Mosphoran Highwaste is known for its oddly shaped rock formations. Some form roofs over the paths, or spires, or any number of other things. Also, right where you're standing is a spring, and resting place for travelers. The spring shrines antedate the Galtean Alliance! There is a lot we don't know about the shrines, though a researcher from Archades is here looking into them. He might be able to tell you more. All this and more awaits you in the Mosphoran Highwaste! / The Mosphoran Highwaste is a rugged, mountainous region, a natural border between Dalmasca and Nabradia. The climate changes greatly from the north to south sides. To the north of Mosphora you have a great forest, to the south a barren desert. This harsh environment kept trade between north and south to a minimum before airships became common. You can appreciate how, in the past, caravans crossing the mountains were vital to the locals' survival. That's the shape of things in the region. Crossing the mountains isn't easy these days, but just think of how hard it used to be! / Hello there! I'm a scout, a guide to this Mosphoran Highwaste. If there's anything you'd like to know, just ask! (choices: How do you get to Archadia? / What are scouts?) / Huh? If you want to go to Archadia, just head north across the Mosphoran Highwaste, then east through the forest beyond. Only problem is, there's been trouble in the forest lately. Some travelers have been turned back. But that's the only way through. / The Mosphoran Highwaste is a mountainous divide with Dalmasca to the south and Nabradia to the north, a different climate on each side. Incidentally, Archadia lies to the east, on the far side of the Salikawood. The gate that way was recently fixed, so you should get through fine.

speaker: Determined Traveler
line_text: My wife and I decided to throw it all away and head to the capital! At least that's what we'd planned... Now I'm not so sure I'll make it in the capital. I mean, what if I fail? I worry, you know... Ah, what to do? / My wife and I decided to throw it all away and go on a journey! We left behind our past and our ties to home, to climb this mountain! ...Where is she, anyway? Last I saw her, she was headed off toward the shrines, saying she was thirsty... / My wife and I decided to throw it all away and head to the capital! But we hear that the road is blocked up ahead... ...Where is she, anyway? Last I saw her, she was headed off toward the shrines, saying she was thirsty... / My wife and I decided to throw it all away and head to the capital! The blocked road is open again, and our new life awaits! What is she doing, anyway? She's been staring at that rock forever!

speaker: Concerned Woman
line_text: My husband! For the love of... I thought we were going to the capital to start a new life!? When did he lose his nerve!? / Did you notice, dear? Of all the shrines on the mountain, only this one has water! / Oh, are you headed to the capital, too? According to our map, we should go northwest from here...but my husband, he cavils and stalls. He says he's concerned about the road ahead being blocked, but why don't we just go and see for ourselves? / Doesn't this giant boulder look like it's about to topple? If one were to push it from the other side...avalanche!

speaker: Concerned Woman
line_text: That was far far far too dangerous! We were almost crushed by that boulder! Exactly as I expected, though! I thought there might be a path on the other side!

speaker: Scout
line_text: Would you like to buy a map, kupo? / What a shame, kupo! You already own all of the maps I have for sale. / Select a map to purchase: (choices: [value][value] / [value][value] / [value][value] / [value][value] / [value][value] / [value][value] / Cancel) / So long, kupo! / Kupo! You don't have enough gil! Sorry, no gil, no map! / A fine purchase, kupo! You won't regret it. Moogle's honor! / Your location map for this area is complete! / Guess what? I saw a giant bomb deep in the Salikawood, kupo! That's not far from the Nabreus Deadlands...it probably came from there! Whatever, you watch yourself, kupo! / Guess what? I saw a giant bomb deep in the Salikawood, kupo! That's not far from the Nabreus Deadlands...it probably came from there! If you're headed towards Archadia, don't get bogged down in Nabudis, kupo! Dangerous place, that! / Guess what? I saw a giant bomb deep in the Salikawood, kupo! That's not far from the Nabreus Deadlands...it probably came from there! I'm sure the one I saw was the Bomb King! I wouldn't want a forest fire to break out, so I'd avoid exciting it, were I you, kupo...

speaker: Craftsmoogle
line_text: I heard the shrines were broken, and the springs dried up. But look at all the water, kupo! I came all the way out here for nothing.

speaker: Craftsmoogle
line_text: Kupo-po-po... I came to fix the shrines, but they're not broken, kupo! I guess I'll just rest here a while.

speaker: Craftsmoogle
line_text: Kupo, you're the one I met by the Salikawood gate! You remember me, the craftsmoogle, kupo? I've come out to check the shrines of Mosphora! Maintaining the ancient buildings of this land is a very important task for us League moogles.
